behavior: Replace generic recursive subset comparison with fixed permission-category comparison using selector/access Maps and Sets.
Validate both response and request against pinned official JSON schemas before comparing grants.

Non-null entries arrays, including empty arrays, override legacy read/write projections; null and omission use legacy rules. Normalize only for comparison and preserve the original response object for native dispatch.

Require exact structural selector matches and nonincreasing positive access; retain every requested deny, and retain every requested read or a deny at that selector while any write remains. Equivalent duplicate rules and reordering are accepted.

Only an effective empty filesystem with no scan-depth Option value is a filesystem refusal. Deny-only, depth-only, and positive responses retain selector/restriction/depth checks. Null and omitted Option depths are equal; any retained nonempty filesystem response must keep the requested effective depth.

Interpret requested network only when network=true is granted and requested filesystem only when a nonempty filesystem response is retained. Complete or per-category refusals remain possible for schema-valid unknown fields in unselected request categories.
Reject unknown fields in every granted permission category and in selected requested categories; do not guess path aliases, glob subsets or cross-platform path equivalence.
Fake-native service regression verifies invalid restriction omissions cause zero respond calls and preserve the pending prompt; a subsequent valid response is forwarded unchanged.
compatibilityChanges: The old service assertion accepting an unrequested globScanMaxDepth=1 for literal legacy reads now expects rejection. Matching depths and null/omitted depth equivalence remain accepted.
Additional unknown permission fields allowed by broad official schemas are rejected when granted or when interpreting a selected requested category; unselected request categories remain declinable.
Scope omission, session scope, and strictAutoReview true/false/null remain schema-compatible.

tests.note: Initial regression revision before later review tightened depth and category handling.
